policy.note: During the Phase 27 freeze, product-code changes require an auditable blocker entry tied to the pull request. Empty is the expected steady state.

blockers.justification: Phase 33 corrects cross-surface identity continuity, preserves existing Nvet roles during CTG One linking, hardens signed Android releases to the canonical production API, and removes legacy mobile branding before Play distribution. These protected product changes address release-blocking account divergence and mobile release consistency defects without authorizing commercial launch.

Phase 34 closes the release-blocking Android identity gap by adding CTG One authorization-code plus PKCE federation, encrypted native verifier/state handling, reliable cold-start callbacks, canonical Nvet session persistence, and exact preservation of Nvet role authority including SUPERADMIN. It also converges the web/mobile visual source of truth without authorizing commercial launch or weakening the frozen payment and external-evidence gates.

Phase 35 hardens the Android artifact that will be evaluated by Google Play: release cleartext transport is denied while emulator-only HTTP remains isolated to debug, R8/minification becomes a tested release invariant, and CTG One federation is incorporated into the Play Data Safety and automated compliance contracts. The phase preserves draft-only Play automation, manual production promotion, operator-owned signing/console evidence, and the independent payment-provider gate.

Phase 36 adds privacy-minimized mobile runtime and CTG One federation observability, release-health SLO evaluation, and explicit integration with the existing append-only beta evidence boundary. These protected changes are required to detect operational regressions before real beta activation while keeping Play Vitals, physical-device evidence, real user cohorts and elapsed observation windows operator-owned and fail-closed.

Phase 37 closes release-blocking dashboard authority and role-convergence defects: ADMIN/SUPERADMIN mobile sessions must not fall through CLIENT navigation, SUPERADMIN must inherit ADMIN capabilities consistently beyond RolesGuard, and the canonical beta control plane must expose the Phase 36 observation-evidence boundary. The phase adds regression certification without authorizing commercial launch, mutating production data, or weakening external payment and operator evidence gates.

Phase 39 remediates the critical/high production dependency findings surfaced by Phase 38, starting with the vulnerable bcrypt/node-pre-gyp/tar installation chain and compatible transitive refreshes. Dependency and lockfile mutations are intentionally isolated behind this audited release-blocker PR, with full backend/mobile/Android/RC regression gates and no authorization of commercial launch, Play publication, provider configuration changes or production database mutation.

Phase 44 closed the process-restart durability gap for idempotent appointment creation and introduced the local recovery record required for a safe financial continuation. Its post-merge P1 review identified that the continuation still needed to be connected to explicit user-confirmed payment resumption, which is tracked by Phase 45 rather than reopening background financial replay.

Phase 45 closes the P1 continuation gap discovered after Phase 44: a booking recovered after process restart now persists an explicit financial handoff and exposes user-confirmed payment resumption from appointment detail. Payments remain excluded from background replay, the original idempotency contract is reused, stale handoffs are discarded when backend transaction state advances, and no provider configuration or commercial launch boundary is changed.

Phase 46 closes a cross-platform release-readiness defect in which persisted React Query and Zustand state was not explicitly owned by one authenticated Nvet user. The phase makes logout/account switching a hard state boundary on web and mobile, purges legacy/unowned caches, disconnects mobile chat and payment-recovery handoffs, and tightens mobile backend reconciliation without adding product functionality or authorizing financial background replay, provider mutation, Play publication or commercial launch.
